newsitem.title: USA: Donna Karan ends pact with Designer Holdings.
newsitem.headline: Donna Karan ends pact with Designer Holdings.

text.p: Donna Karan International Inc. said Wednesday the fashion house and Designer Holdings Ltd. have mutually agreed to terminate a licensing agreement for DKNY Jeans.
Designer Holdings, a clothing manufacturer, had paid Donna Karan $6 million to design, start up and develop the new line of jeans, as well as $1.26 million in advance royalties.
As a result of the termination, Donna Karan will reverse a $6 million gain recognised in the third quarter of 1996.

Donna Karan said it will purchase all sales and marketing plans, patterns, samples, fabrics, and other materials developed in connection with the jeanswear business. It will recognise these expenses in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The companies called off the deal because of difficulties coordinating the design schedule of Donna Karan with the manufacturing schedule of Designer Holdings, it said.

"In addition, the companies were unable to agree on the extent of the product line necessary to be competitive in the jeanswear market and therefore, both parties felt that it was in their best interests to terminate the license agreement," said Stephen Ruzow, Donna Karan's president and chief operating officer.
Ruzow said DKNY Jeans is an important part of its growth strategy and Donna Karan is committed to building the DKNY Jeanswear brand in-house.

Donna Karan designs, markets and distributes "designer" and "bridge" collections of women's and men's apparel, sportswear, accessories and shoes under the Donna Karan New York and DKNY brand names, respectively.
Donna Karan's stock fell 50 cents to $11.25, while Designer Holdings rose 50 cents to $12.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
